checks.why: Without CPR SpO2 falls about 0.1 %/s and there is no restart chance at all. Compress first, then bring the AED.
VF is shockable. A shock multiplies the CPR success chance by up to 1.7 for about 70 s.
Analyze (stop compressions: the AED detects motion), then shock when advised and go straight back to CPR.

checks.text: No shock on a patient with a pulse
checks.why: A shock on a beating heart causes asystole and cardiac arrest.
Only IV epinephrine counts toward CPR success (up to x2); IM and autoinjectors do not. Use an IO if there is no IV.
Continuous CPR for more than a minute, a recent shock, IV epinephrine and the best-trained compressor give the best odds.
After ROSC keep the airway open and ventilate until oxygen recovers.
